title: Strict principal reduction cones and their compatible cone comparisons
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ finite with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\pi$, and $X$ any scheme. Put $R=\mathcal O_{E,X}=p_X^*\underline{\mathcal O_E}$, with the coefficient sheaves of [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Use unbounded cochain complexes of $R$-module sheaves and the cone, shift and localization conventions of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For $n\ge1$ define $D_n(M)=\operatorname{Cone}(\pi^n:M\to M)$, with diagonal maps on chain maps, transition $D_{n+1}(M)\to D_n(M)$ given by $(x,y)\mapsto(x,\pi y)$, and coaugmentation $j_n:M\to D_n(M)$ given by $m\mapsto(m,0)$. This is a functorial strict model of the derived reduction tower of [sk-def-pe-derived-completion]: writing $K_n=K\otimes^{\mathbf L}_R(\mathcal O_E/\pi^n)_X$, regarded as an $R$-module object by restriction of scalars, there are isomorphisms $QD_n(M)\cong(QM)_n$ in $D(R)$, natural in $M$, carrying $QD_n$ of the transition to the canonical transition $K_{n+1}\to K_n$ and $Q(j_n)$ to the canonical reduction map $K\to K_n$. Each $D_n$ preserves quasi-isomorphisms and induces an additive exact endofunctor of $D(R)$. For a chain map $f:A\to B$ its cone comparison
$$D_n(\operatorname{Cone}(f))\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Cone}(D_n(f))$$
is $(b,a,b',a')\mapsto(b,b',a,-a')$ in the ordered coordinates $B^q,A^{q+1},B^{q+1},A^{q+2}$. The shift comparison $D_n(M[r])\xrightarrow{\sim}D_n(M)[r]$ is $(x,y)\mapsto(x,(-1)^r y)$ for every integer $r$. These comparisons are natural, commute with all tower transitions, preserve cone inclusions and the boundary after the shift comparison, and carry $j_{\operatorname{Cone}(f)}$ to the cone map of $(j_A,j_B)$ and $j_{M[r]}$ to $j_M[r]$.

source.place: Cones paragraph, first two sentences and the cone/shift commutation sentence; explicit strict principal-reduction comparison. Supporting cone convention: Stacks Tag 014E (definition-cone).

proof.text: Write $t_n=\pi^n$. By [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], $D_n(M)^q=M^q\oplus M^{q+1}$ with $d_n(x,y)=(d_Mx+t_ny,-d_My)$. Its square is zero since $d_Mt_n=t_nd_M$. For $g:M\to N$, put $D_n(g)(x,y)=(gx,gy)$; the chain-map equation, identities, composition and addition hold componentwise. The transition $T_n(x,y)=(x,\pi y)$ is a chain map because $t_n\pi=t_{n+1}$; its composites give all tower arrows. Also $d_n(m,0)=(d_Mm,0)$, so $j_n$ is a chain map. The equations $T_nj_{n+1}=j_n$ and naturality of $T_n,j_n$ are componentwise identities. No multiplication on $M$ is assumed injective.

source.place: Cones, first two sentences: strict reduction functors and tower

proof.text: If $g:M\to N$ is a quasi-isomorphism, its two copies and $D_n(g)$ give a morphism between the scalar cone triangles of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]: inclusion and projection commute with the diagonal map. In $D(R)$ the first two components $Qg$ are isomorphisms, so [lem-sf-triangle-morphism-iso] makes $QD_n(g)$ an isomorphism. The cohomology functors factoring through $Q$ in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] then show that $D_n(g)$ is a quasi-isomorphism. The localization property in that definition therefore descends $QD_n$ to an endofunctor $F_n$ of $D(R)$ and descends $T_n,j_n$ to natural transformations. For additivity, rearranging the four summands identifies $D_n(M\oplus N)$ with $D_n(M)\oplus D_n(N)$ and preserves each inclusion and projection. The additive structure on the derived category induced from complexes in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] makes these localized diagrams biproduct diagrams. Every derived object is represented by a complex, so $F_n$ preserves zero and binary biproducts. The identity $f+g=\nabla(f\oplus g)\Delta$, with diagonal $\Delta$ and codiagonal $\nabla$ determined by these diagrams, now proves additivity.

source.place: Cones: representative independence and additive descent

proof.text: Put $B_n=(\mathcal O_E/\pi^n)_X$ and let $P_n$ have $R$ in degrees $-1,0$, differential $t_n$, and augmentation $\epsilon_n:P_n\to B_n[0]$ equal to reduction in degree zero. Exactness of the coefficient sequence in [det-pe-derived-nakayama-resolution] says precisely that $\epsilon_n$ is a quasi-isomorphism: its only cohomology is $B_n$ in degree zero. Each term is flat, since the maps $R\otimes_RN\to N$, $a\otimes z\mapsto az$, and $z\mapsto1\otimes z$ are inverse; hence tensor by $R$ is the identity and is exact. On a small site model of $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$, [lem-weil-pbc-independent-bounded-flat-kflat] makes $P_n$ K-flat (it is zero outside degrees $-1,0$). The same argument applies to $R[0]$.

source.place: Cones: the specified two-term coefficient resolution; Stacks Tag 06YQ (lemma-bounded-flat-K-flat)

proof.text: For any $M$, choose $u:C\to M$ K-flat with flat terms by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. By [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent], $QC\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}QP_n$ is computed by $\operatorname{Tot}(C\otimes_RP_n)$. The signed interchange $c\otimes p\mapsto(-1)^{ij}p\otimes c$ in bidegree $(i,j)$ identifies this with $\operatorname{Tot}(P_n\otimes_RC)$: in the total differential [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], the two signs on the $d_C$ term are $(-1)^{(i+1)j}$ and $(-1)^{ij+j}$, and those on the $d_P$ term are $(-1)^{i+i(j+1)}$ and $(-1)^{ij}$, respectively. They agree. In degree $q$ the latter total is $C^q\oplus C^{q+1}$ and its differential is $(x,y)\mapsto(d_Cx+t_ny,-d_Cy)$, so it is $D_n(C)$. The augmentation $QP_n\cong B_n[0]$ and the invertible $QD_n(u)$ from step 2 yield $QD_n(M)\cong(QM)_n$. All these identifications are natural on the K-flat flat-term resolving category; its localization equivalence and natural-transformation extension in [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] extend them naturally to $D(R)$. This gives one family of comparisons, rather than separately chosen triangulated cones.

source.place: Cones, first two sentences: tensor computation and natural comparison

proof.text: The coefficient quotient $B_{n+1}\to B_n$ lifts to $v_n:P_{n+1}\to P_n$ whose degree $-1$ map is multiplication by $\pi$ and degree zero map is the identity. Indeed $t_n\pi=t_{n+1}$, and $\epsilon_nv_n$ is the quotient composed with $\epsilon_{n+1}$. The reduction $R\to B_n$ lifts to $e_n:R[0]\to P_n$ by the identity in degree zero; $\epsilon_ne_n$ is reduction and $v_ne_{n+1}=e_n$. After the signed interchange of step 4, $v_n\otimes1_C$ is exactly $(x,y)\mapsto(x,\pi y)$, while $e_n\otimes1_C$ is $c\mapsto(c,0)$. Naturality in both variables and the extension uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] therefore identify $QT_n$ with the canonical derived quotient transition, and $Qj_n$ with the canonical reduction map of [sk-def-pe-derived-completion]. These are maps of underlying $R$-objects, so no exactness of ordinary reduction on $M$ is used.

source.place: Cones: compatibility with the coefficient quotient maps and the canonical reduction maps

proof.text:
Let $f:A\to B$ and write $(b,a,b',a')$ for $D_n(\operatorname{Cone}(f))^q$. Using the cone differential of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], its differential is
$$(d_Bb+fa+t_nb',\ -d_Aa+t_na',\ -d_Bb'-fa',\ d_Aa').$$
Under $\Phi_n(b,a,b',a')=(b,b',a,-a')$, this becomes
$$(d_Bb+fa+t_nb',\ -d_Bb'-fa',\ -d_Aa+t_na',\ -d_Aa').$$
This is also the differential of $(b,b',a,-a')$ in $\operatorname{Cone}(D_n(f))$. The inverse permutation is $(u,v,w,z)\mapsto(u,w,v,-z)$, so $\Phi_n$ is a chain isomorphism with precisely the formula asserted.

source.place: Cones: explicit cone interchange; Stacks Tag 014E (definition-cone)

proof.text: For $r\in\mathbf Z$, put $e=(-1)^r$. The source differential on $D_n(M[r])$ is $(x,y)\mapsto(e\,d_Mx+t_ny,-e\,d_My)$. Applying $S_r(x,y)=(x,e y)$ gives $(e\,d_Mx+t_ny,-d_My)$. The target differential on $D_n(M)[r]$ applied to $(x,e y)$ is the same pair, since $e^2=1$. Thus $S_r$ is an isomorphism, with inverse the same sign change. The formula $(-1)^{r+s}=(-1)^r(-1)^s$ gives the coherence of these shift comparisons, including negative shifts; $S_0$ is the identity. These use the integer shifts of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

source.place: Cones: shift commutation sentence and all integer shifts

proof.text: Every square of chain maps between $f:A\to B$ and $\widetilde f:\widetilde A\to\widetilde B$ acts on the four coordinates by its $B,A,B,A$ maps. These commute with the permutation and minus sign in $\Phi_n$, proving its naturality; two copies of a chain map likewise commute with $S_r$. Applying $T_n$ before $\Phi_n$ gives $(b,\pi b',a,-\pi a')$, which is its value after the cone map of $(T_n(A),T_n(B))$. Also $T_nS_r(x,y)=S_rT_n(x,y)=(x,(-1)^r\pi y)$. Hence both comparisons commute with the whole tower (adjacent-transition commutation implies commutation with their composites).

source.place: Cones: naturality and tower compatibility of the explicit comparisons

proof.text: For the cone inclusion $i:B\to\operatorname{Cone}(f)$, $\Phi_nD_n(i)(b,b')=(b,b',0,0)$, the cone inclusion of $D_n(f)$. For the boundary $-p:\operatorname{Cone}(f)\to A[1]$ of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], $D_n(-p)(b,a,b',a')=(-a,-a')$ and then $S_1$ gives $(-a,a')$. This equals the cone boundary applied to $\Phi_n(b,a,b',a')$, so the boundary square has the required sign. Finally $\Phi_nj_{\operatorname{Cone}(f)}(b,a)=(b,0,a,0)$, exactly the cone map of $(j_A,j_B)$, and $S_rj_{M[r]}(m)=(m,0)=j_M[r](m)$. These identities also prove compatibility of the coaugmentations with the displayed comparisons.

source.place: Cones: inclusions, negative-projection boundary and coaugmentation squares

proof.text: By [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], every distinguished triangle is isomorphic to the image of a chain-map cone triangle. Steps 6 and 9 identify the image under $F_n$ of such a triangle with the cone triangle of $D_n(f)$, using $\Phi_n$ on its third object and $S_1$ on its shifted first object. It is therefore distinguished. Step 7 supplies the natural shift isomorphism after localization, and step 2 supplies additivity. This is exactly the definition of an exact endofunctor in [def-weil-triangulated-category]. Together with steps 4–5 and 8–9 it proves every clause of the strict derived-reduction tower assertion.

source.place: Cones and Isomorphisms: passage from the explicit strict comparisons to exactness
